issue.title: Cross-account take visibility, ownership, and attribution on shared devices
issue.body:
### Problem statement

Recordings are stored per verse with no creator identity. `recordings` (`src/db/schema.ts`) links only to `bible_text_id` — there is no `recorded_by_user_id`. Account switching (`switchToDeviceAccount` in `src/services/accountSession.ts`) swaps the token and `active_user_id` but does not clear, namespace, or filter local recordings or audio files.

Consequences on a shared device:

- User B sees User A's take as the current draft, with no indication A recorded it.
- B recording demotes A's take (`addRecordingTake` clears `is_latest` for the whole verse — `src/db/recordingsRepository.ts`).
- B can play or delete A's take with no ownership check.
- Uploads use whichever token is active (`src/services/recordingSync.ts`), so A's pending take can be uploaded and attributed to B (`uploadedBy` is derived server-side from the bearer).

This is a data-integrity and attribution problem, not a Record Tab UI problem. **#71 stays scoped to single-user multi-take UI.**

### User scenario

A translator records a take on a shared phone, hands it to a colleague, who switches to their own account and records their own take of the same passage.

### Expected behavior

**Product decision (confirmed):** default is **show my takes only**. Showing another user's takes is an explicit team/review mode, never the default.

- Every take is owned by the user who captured it.
- Default Review list shows only the active user's takes.
- Teammate takes appear only in an explicit team/review mode, always with visible creator attribution.
- Another user's unsynced takes never silently appear as the current user's draft.
- Recording as B does not demote or alter A's take set.
- A's pending takes upload under A's identity, even if B is the active account when the upload runs.
- By default a user cannot select-as-draft, delete, or upload a take they did not record.

### Technical findings (from implementation review)

| Area | Current state | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Creator identity | Absent | `src/db/schema.ts`; `RecordingRow` in `src/types/db/types.ts` |
| Take scoping | Verse only | `addRecordingTake`, `getTakesForVerse`, `getLatestRecordingForVerse` |
| Account switch | Auth only; DB and files retained | `accountSession.ts`, `authSession.ts` |
| Upload identity | Active bearer at upload time | `recordingSync.ts`; `uploadedBy` in `src/types/api/verseAudio.ts` |
| Server model | One blob per `(projectUnitId, bibleTextId)`, PUT replaces | `docs/guides/recordings-sync-contract.md` |
| Pending counts | Not user-scoped | `getPendingUploadCount` (`src/db/queries.ts`) |
| UI metadata | Take number only; no creator | `src/components/ui/DraftTakeRow.tsx` |
| Known gap | Already documented in code | `src/db/recordingsRepository.ts` — "Shared-device `(bible_text_id, user_id)` scoping lands with #99/#105" |

### Relationship to #256

Conflict detection in #256 assumes server-side attribution is trustworthy — that a take flagged as conflicting can be traced to who recorded it. That is not true today: a take captured by A can arrive at the server as B's. Ownership must land before conflict resolution can present "A's take vs B's take" correctly. This ticket is a **prerequisite for #256 behaving correctly on shared devices**, not a duplicate of it.

### Proposed scope

1. Land #105: `recorded_by_user_id` migration, stamped from `getActiveUserId()` at capture, upload under the owner's stored credentials.
2. Scope `is_latest` and `take_number` per `(bible_text_id, recorded_by_user_id)` so one user's takes cannot demote another's.
3. Filter take reads and pending-upload aggregates by active user.
4. Add the explicit team/review mode with creator attribution (name or initials via existing `users` table and `getAccountDisplayName`).
5. Enforce ownership rules on select, delete, and upload.
6. Define backfill policy for pre-migration rows with no owner.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] New takes persist `recorded_by_user_id` at capture.
- [ ] After A → B switch, B's Review shows only B's takes by default.
- [ ] B recording does not clear or alter `is_latest` within A's take set.
- [ ] A's pending takes upload with A's credentials; server `uploadedBy` matches A regardless of active account.
- [ ] B cannot select, delete, or upload A's take outside an explicit, attributed flow.
- [ ] Team/review mode shows takes from multiple users with creator attribution on each row.
- [ ] Sign-out or switch does not destroy other known accounts' local takes or pending uploads.
- [ ] Pending upload counts and sync indicators reflect the active user's work.
- [ ] Unit tests cover attribution at capture, per-user scoping, filtered reads, and upload credential selection.
- [ ] Android device QA with two accounts recorded on the PR (mic + filesystem + account switching).

### Product decisions still needed

- Where does team/review mode live — Record tab toggle, separate screen, or drafting surface?
- Which roles may enter team/review mode (peer checker only, or any project member)?
- May a peer checker act on another user's take, and if so which actions?
- Attribution display: full name, initials, or role label?
- Backfill: treat ownerless legacy takes as belonging to the active user, or leave unattributed and read-only?

### Edge cases

- Take recorded offline, account switched before upload.
- Same person with two accounts or differing display names on one device.
- Legacy rows with `recorded_by_user_id = NULL`.
- Two users with pending takes for the same `bible_text_id` (server currently keeps one blob — last PUT wins until #256).
- Paused-take markers are stored under a single global KV key (`PAUSED_TAKES_KV_KEY` in `src/services/pausedTakes.ts`) and are not user-scoped.
- Account removed from the device while its recordings and files remain.
- `deleteRecordingTake` does not delete the audio file today, so ownership filtering must not orphan files.

### Risks

- Privacy: unrelated accounts sharing a community phone should not see each other's drafts by default.
- Misattribution: uploading under the wrong token corrupts server-side authorship and undermines #256.
- Silent data loss: per-user `is_latest` scoping changes existing invariants; needs careful migration.
- Server model: one blob per unit/verse limits true multi-contributor history until #256 lands.
- Scope creep: must stay out of #71.

### Dependencies

- **#105** — required (ownership column, owner-token upload)
- **#118** — parent epic
- **#103 / #110** — migration framework and schema hardening
- **#71** — take list UI this filters into (do not expand #71)
- **#256** — consumes reliable attribution; sequenced after
- Account switcher (#84–#87) — already shipped

### Testing

- **Unit:** capture attribution, per-user `is_latest` and `take_number`, filtered reads, upload credential selection, pending-count scoping.
- **Component:** default vs team mode rendering with attribution.
- **Device (required):** two accounts, record → switch → record → upload → verify `uploadedBy`, plus permission gates on delete and select.
- **Gates:** `npm run format:check && npm run lint && npm run typecheck && npm test -- --ci`

### Estimated complexity

**Large** — schema migration, sync and upload identity, permission rules, new UI mode, and multi-account device QA.

### Links

- Epic: #118
- Required dependency: #105
- Related: #71 (single-user multi-take UI — out of scope), #256 (conflict detection), #99 / #103

## API readiness note (board audit — refreshed)

**Why the API is not complete for this ticket**

Cross-account attribution on shared devices has two layers. Local ownership (#105-style `recorded_by_user_id`, per-user take scoping, owner-token upload) can land in mobile without new fluent-api routes. **Server-side attribution and team/review sync are still incomplete on fluent-api `main`.**

### What exists today (fluent-api `main` @ `28f9bdb`, 2026-08-06)

- No `verse-audio` / `recordings` domain on `main`. Domains remain: languages, bibles, projects, chapter-assignments, translated-verses, pericopes, USFM, AI, etc.
- Cloudflare R2 blob storage landed for **USFM export** only (`src/lib/blob-storage.ts`, #212) — not verse recordings.
- Open [fluent-api PR #224](https://github.com/eten-tech-foundation/fluent-api/pull/224) (`feat/verse-audio`, tip `d6f3190`, still **unmerged**): `PUT/GET/DELETE /verse-audio/{projectUnitId}/{bibleTextId}` + chapter list; `uploadedBy` from bearer; **one blob per `(projectUnitId, bibleTextId)`** (re-upload replaces). Competing [PR #188](https://github.com/eten-tech-foundation/fluent-api/pull/188) still open.

### What is missing / incomplete

1. **Merged + deployed verse-audio API** — until #224 (or chosen successor) is on `main`/prod, live `uploadedBy` verification and cross-account download of teammate takes cannot be DevQA’d against a real server.
2. **Multi-contributor history** — #224’s uniqueness invariant keeps a single server recording per verse. Team/review mode that needs both A’s and B’s server-side takes (or conflict pairs for #256) is **not** supported; last PUT wins.
3. **No “list takes by user” / multi-take model** — no API for per-user take stacks, take numbers, or non-destructive concurrent uploads.

### What needs to be done (fluent-api)

1. Merge/deploy verse-audio (#224 vs #188 decision) so mobile can upload with the correct owner bearer and read `uploadedBy`.
2. Product/API decision: stay with one-blob-per-verse (document that team mode is **local-device only** until a multi-take model exists) **or** extend the schema to store multiple takes / contributors per verse.
3. If multi-take is required for #256 conflict UX, file/implement a fluent-api follow-up (history table or take_id) before promising server-backed team review.

**Mobile can proceed on:** local schema/scoping + owner credentials for upload. Do not block local AC on unmerged API; mock only for UI demos without #224 deployed.

Checked against fluent-api `main` @ `28f9bdb` (2026-08-06). Prior audit was `3ef4025` (2026-07-31).
